answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake bond before it can trade, locked in a shared registry. An operator trying to build an island of fake identities must fund every one, so creating thousands of personas costs thousands of bonds, while an honest agent pays only once. A violet flag on coordinated behavior triggers a challenge: the suspect must prove distinct work histories or forfeit its bond. To forge each new identity therefore carries a real, upfront price, making mass fakery economically irrational instead of free.
